resources.string: You are already acting as another user. Return to your own account first.
You are acting as #VAR1#. Everything you do is done in the name of this user and marked in the change history. Your own account is #VAR2#; you will be returned to it automatically at #VAR3#.
Messages and emails cannot be sent while you act as another user. Return to your own account to send them in your own name.
Single sign-on is not available while you act as another user, so that no other application is logged in with the identity of this user. Return to your own account first.
Do you want to act as #VAR1#? Until you return to your own account, Admidio behaves exactly as if #VAR1# had logged in. Every change you make is marked in the change history.

Lets administrators act as another user, to see exactly what that user sees. A link in the contacts list switches the session to the user, and logging out returns the administrator to their own account. Every change made meanwhile is marked in the change history, and every impersonation is recorded.
Every time an administrator of this organization acted as another user. The most recent 500 are shown.
No administrator has acted as another user yet.
Your return to your own account could not be verified. For safety reasons you have been logged out.
Counted from the moment the administrator starts acting as another user. When it has passed, the administrator is returned to their own account automatically.
An administrator is acting as you in #VAR1#

Hello #VAR1#, the administrator #VAR2# started acting as you in #VAR3# at #VAR4#, usually to find out why something does not work for you. Changes made meanwhile are marked in the change history. If you did not expect this, please contact the administrators of #VAR3#.
Sends the user an email when an administrator starts acting as them. Users without an email address are not notified.
Administrators who may act as other users
Only administrators can act as other users. If roles are selected here instead of all administrators, only administrators who are members of at least one of these roles can do so.
You are back in your own account.

If this is enabled, an administrator can only act as a user whose roles the administrator either shares or administers. This prevents acting as a user who has rights in another organization that the administrator does not have.
This contact has no active account that could be used.

This user is a member of roles in another organization that you neither share nor administer. Acting as this user would give you rights you do not have. This can be allowed in the preferences of the plugin.
This user is not a member of the current organization.
The time limit for acting as another user has passed. You are back in your own account.
